title: Mock Data Contract
description: Single source of truth for entity field shapes + variant counts + relationships. Produced by a Beat 1 agent from the PRD's data schema section; consumed by `scaffold-types` (emits src/lib/types.ts) and `scaffold-mock-data` (emits src/lib/mock-data/<entity>.ts skeletons with type-safe placeholder arrays). Per-entity agents in Beat 3 fill values via Edit; field shapes can't drift because the script pinned them.

sharedEnums.description: Reusable enum types referenced by entity fields via { kind: 'enum', enumName: '<name>' }. Emitted at the top of src/lib/types.ts.

name.description: camelCase entity name. Becomes the TS interface (PascalCased), the mock-data filename, and the aggregator key.

tsInterfaceName.description: Optional override for the TS interface name. Defaults to PascalCase(name).

idConvention.description: Pattern for the entity's id field. E.g. "ge-001" or "sub-velatinib". The script seeds N placeholder ids matching this pattern.

variantCounts.description: How many records the scaffolded skeleton arrays should contain per variant.

relationships.description: Foreign-key style links to other entities. Documented, not enforced by the script — the value-filling agent uses them to choose realistic ids.

references.description: Entity name (must match one of the entities[].name in this contract).

notes.description: Free-form voice/domain notes the value-filling agent should follow. E.g. 'Use real eCTD module codes; no marketing voice.'

enumName.description: Required when kind='enum'. Must match a key in sharedEnums OR be inlined via literalValues.

literalValues.description: Required when kind='literalUnion'. Inline string literal union.

referencesEntity.description: Optional when kind='id': declares which entity's id this is. Documentary only.

example.description: One realistic sample value the script uses as the placeholder seed. Agents replace these with real values via Edit.

constraint.description: Free-form constraint note for the value-filling agent. E.g. '≤ 80 chars', '0–100', 'ISO 8601'.
